records.title: Ramapo Housing and Residence Life › Laurel Hall - Residence Life › Laurel Hall Building Features
records.content:
### Laurel Hall Building Features

Laurel Hall shares the quad with Pine Hall, and is near to the Scott Student Center, Birch Tree Inn and the Atrium. Laurel Hall is a 432-bed suite-style residence that contains four single bedrooms, a bathroom with stall shower and a small common area. The community space has a kitchenette-type unit with a sink, microwave and full-size refrigerator along with some storage space for food items; a small table with four chairs, a couch, club chair, coffee table, and TV cart. Each bedroom has an adjustable long twin bed that can be raised to captain’s height, mattress, three-drawer chest, desk with movable pedestal drawer unit (can be used as a night table), task chair on casters, overhead bookcase storage unit (seven feet wide), tack board, and wardrobe with two doors (half hanging clothes and half shelves), desk and desk chair. Each bedroom door is accessed through student ID card for to the resident of the bedroom. Hall office on first floor. Screening room, kitchen for resident use, and game room on the first floor. Outdoor basketball and volleyball courts with picnic area and grills. First and second floor lounge space.

records.content:
### Bischoff Hall Building Features

Bischoff Hall is adjacent to the Trustees Pavilion. A five-story building, with elevator access, houses about 250 students in hotel-like large rooms, configured for two resident students. Furnishings include bed, mattress, large desk with rolling pedestal storage unit, desk, desk chair, overhead bookcase/storage, tack board, chest of drawers, wardrobe, and bookcase/storage unit are provided in each bedroom; Flat screen televisions and Wi-Fi in all floor lounges Hall office on first floor Outdoor amphitheater-like seating Outdoor picnic area and grills State-of-the-art gaming equipment in fourth-floor lounges in both residence halls Bischoff Hall is designated as dry (alcohol prohibited) regardless of age. Bedroom, approx. 14’-7” x 15′ Bischoff Hall residents are required to have meal plans.

fields.title: Hispanic Latinx Heritage Celebration
fields.organizer: The Multicultural Center and the Office of Access, Belonging and Community (ABC)
fields.description: The Multicultural Center and Office of Access, Belonging, and Community, in collaboration with SHPE, ALMA, Latinx Pre-Law Society, OLU, and ALPFA, invite the Ramapo College community to celebrate the start of Hispanic Latinx Heritage Month! This year’s theme, Aprovecha hoy. Crea tu mañana., celebrates the experiences, aspirations, and contributions of the Hispanic and Latinx community. Join us for the official Presidential Proclamation, followed by a special plática between Paola Guevara, Academic Advisor, and Naydelin Reyes Rodriguez ’25, Global People Partner Specialist at S&P Global, reflecting on culture, community, and career development. Refreshments will be served beginning at 1:00 p.m. and will remain available following the stage program.

fields.title: Crystal Queer Tarot
fields.description: Drop-in for Crystal Queer Tarot, a weekly do-it-yourself space for exploring tarot as a wellness ritual — a creative, mindful way to explore your thoughts and emotions and support mental well-being. Studies show practicing tarot can bring comfort, clarity, and meaning in uncertain times. Whether you are new to tarot or a seasoned reader, this space offers an opportunity to reflect and engage using the cards as tools for self-discovery, self-care, and community building. We’ll have a variety of decks and guidebooks by queer, trans, and women tarotists to inspire your interpretations. From the tarot-curious to the tarot expert, everyone is welcome. Questions or accommodation requests? Please email women@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7468.

fields.title: Quiet Together — Silent Book Club & Silent Space
fields.description: Pause and spend some quiet time in community at the Women’s Center. Quiet Together — Silent Book Club & Silent Space is a weekly evening space to read, study, work, rest, or simply be. From 6–6:30 pm, Silent Book Club participants can settle in, socialize, and share what they’re reading. From 6:30–7:30 pm, the Center becomes a shared quiet space open to everyone, whether you’re participating in Silent Book Club or looking for an hour of peace and quiet. From 7:30–8 pm, participants and Center visitors can optionally talk about their quiet-hour activities. Whether you’re looking for a cozy place to read, a calm space to work, or a chance to decompress, come as you are and enjoy being quietly together. Questions or accommodation requests? Email women@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7468.
